core.title: The journey router's route map keeps direct user/system flow routes when flow router routes are added
core.given: The journey router (the composition root) has a route map with at least one flow router route object - an entry that carries a flow router reference and the location of its definition instead of naming the user/system flow directly
core.when: you add or change route-map entries or their dispatch in the composition root
core.then: The route map MUST accept both a direct user/system flow reference and a flow router route object, and existing direct mappings MUST stay valid.
prefer: A mixed route map: direct actions map straight to their user/system flow reference, while interlocked actions map to a flow router route object (flow router reference plus the location of its definition)
avoid: Converting, removing or rejecting existing direct user/system flow mappings when you add flow router routes
unless: The route map declares no flow router route object: a journey router with only direct routes carries no flow router obligation
core.why: The flow router route is additive, so the existing direct mapping remains valid. The user/system flow executor executes the user/system flow in both cases; the runner-delegation part of this convention enforces that.
evidence: The route map and its dispatch accept both direct user/system flow references and flow router route objects
Existing direct mappings still resolve to their user/system flows. Direct entries do not have to be present: a flow-router-only map is acceptable
verification: Source statement (normative MUST): the journey router MUST support both direct and interlocking-enabled routing, and the route map MUST admit a direct user/system flow reference AND a flow router route object. This requires support for both forms, not that both kinds of entry be present.

The automated findings for the sibling parts of this convention (unlinked flow router, missing user/system flow delegation) do not cover this part; check it by reviewing the route-map declaration and its dispatch. Which construct is inspected and how the route forms are recognized is the per-stack checker's concern.
Scope: the composition root only (local name and path from the profile); nothing outside that role fires.

values: the composition root's route map contains at least one flow router route object

fires: A task adds a flow router route to a route map that already has direct entries
A task adds the first flow router route to a route map that has no direct entries
An agent edits route-map handling in a composition root that already holds flow router routes
doesNotFire: The route map holds only direct user/system flow references
Files that do not play the composition-root role

neutralityNotes: ATDD vocabulary (journey router, user/system flow, flow router, route map) is treated as framework-neutral, per the neutral rule id coder.journey-router.flow-router-routing-route-forms; the stack's local names and shapes come from the profile (roles.composition_root.name/path, urn.user-system-flow, idiom.routing#route_map). The concrete route-map construct (JOURNEY_MAP, {flowRouterId, path}, the mixed-map example) has no neutral wording and is carried by the proposed idiom.routing#route_map key plus the Bun reference example in bun.json. FlowRunner/FlowRouterRunner are named only at role level (user/system flow executor, flow router resolver) because the call model itself is the sibling runner-delegation part. Stack applicability gating (typescript/javascript, the atdd.workspace.bun workspace note, and the 'Non-Bun stacks' doesNotFire entry) is per-realization and stays bunOnly; the neutral doesNotFire covers it as 'files that do not play the composition-root role'.
